question: The executive power of the Union is formally vested in the President by which Article of the Constitution?
explanation: Article 52 merely declares that there shall be a President of India; Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President, exercisable directly or through officers subordinate to him.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.text: the elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and of the UTs of Delhi and Puducherry
all members of Parliament and all members of State Legislatures
the members of the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies only

explanation: Under Article 54, the electoral college comprises elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, including (by the 70th Amendment) the Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members are excluded.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: With reference to the election of the President under Article 55, consider the following statements: 1. The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. 2. As far as practicable, there shall be uniformity in the scale of representation of the different States. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Article 55 mandates proportional representation by single transferable vote with voting by secret ballot, and expressly seeks, as far as practicable, uniformity in the scale of representation of different States as well as parity between the States as a whole and the Union.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: To be eligible for election as President, a person must, among other conditions, be qualified for election as a member of which House?
explanation: Article 58 requires that the candidate be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and be at least 35 years of age.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be eligible for election as President of India is:
explanation: Article 58 fixes the minimum age for the office of President at 35 years, the same as for the Vice-President.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: Consider the following statements regarding the impeachment of the President under Article 61: 1. The charge may be preferred by either House of Parliament. 2. The resolution to prefer the charge must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of that House. 3. Nominated members of Parliament cannot participate in the impeachment process. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Impeachment for violation of the Constitution can be initiated in either House, needs a 14-day notice signed by one-fourth of members, and must be passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership. Nominated members, though barred from the President's election, DO participate in impeachment; elected members of State Assemblies do not. Hence statement 3 is wrong.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: There is no constitutional bar on the re-election of a person to the office of President. A sitting President is eligible for re-election:
explanation: Unlike the US (two-term limit under the 22nd Amendment), the Indian Constitution places no limit on the number of times a person may be re-elected as President.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: Consider the following statements about the pardoning powers of the President (Article 72) and the Governor (Article 161): 1. The President can grant pardon in cases where the punishment is by a court-martial. 2. The President can pardon a sentence of death. 3. The Governor of a State can also pardon a sentence of death. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The President's power under Article 72 extends to court-martial cases and to death sentences. The Governor's power under Article 161 does NOT extend to court-martial and does not include pardon of a death sentence (the Governor may suspend, remit or commute, but the power to pardon a death sentence rests with the President). Statement 3 is therefore wrong.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of which body?
explanation: Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States); he is not a member of either House.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)
micro_topic: Vice-President as Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64)

question: With reference to the electoral college that elects the Vice-President, consider the following: 1. It consists of the members of both Houses of Parliament. 2. It includes the nominated members of Parliament. 3. Members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in the election. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of BOTH Houses of Parliament, including nominated members. State legislatures play no part. Hence statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is wrong.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: Which Article provides that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People?
explanation: Article 75(3) embodies collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha. Article 74 deals with the Council aiding and advising the President, Article 77 with conduct of business, and Article 78 with the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India: 1. He is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President. 2. He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court. 3. He has the right to speak and to vote in both Houses of Parliament. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Under Article 76 the Attorney General is appointed by the President, holds office during pleasure, and must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge. He enjoys the right to speak in both Houses and their committees but has NO right to vote. Statement 3 is therefore wrong.
subject: Polity
theme: Union Executive - President, Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers (Laxmikanth)

question: NITI Aayog, which replaced the erstwhile Planning Commission, was established on:
explanation: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) was set up on 1 January 2015 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet, replacing the Planning Commission.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog: 1. It is a constitutional body. 2. The Prime Minister is its ex-officio Chairperson. 3. It has the power to allocate funds to the States. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: NITI Aayog is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body; it was created by executive resolution and functions as a policy think-tank. The Prime Minister chairs it. Unlike the Planning Commission, it has no power to allocate funds. Only statement 2 is correct.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)
micro_topic: Nature and composition of NITI Aayog

question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out across India with effect from:
explanation: GST, introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, came into force nationwide on 1 July 2017, subsuming a range of central and state indirect taxes.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework given statutory backing in 2016, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation target set for the Reserve Bank of India is:

options.text: 2 per cent with a band of plus or minus 2 per cent
4 per cent with a band of plus or minus 2 per cent
5 per cent with a band of plus or minus 1 per cent
6 per cent with a band of plus or minus 2 per cent

explanation: Following the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, the Centre notified a CPI inflation target of 4 per cent with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 per cent (i.e., 2 to 6 per cent), a framework retained for successive five-year periods.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: The single, consolidated law that overhauled India's insolvency resolution process, creating a time-bound framework and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, was enacted in:
explanation: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) was enacted in 2016, consolidating the framework for insolvency resolution of companies and individuals and establishing the IBBI as the regulator.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC): 1. It has six members. 2. Three members are from the Reserve Bank of India and three are appointed by the Central Government. 3. In the event of a tie, the Governor of the RBI has a second or casting vote. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The MPC is a six-member body: three from the RBI (Governor, a Deputy Governor and one RBI officer) and three external members appointed by the Central Government. Decisions are by majority, and in case of a tie the Governor exercises a casting vote. All three statements are correct.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: The demonetisation of the existing 500 and 1000 rupee currency notes was announced on:
explanation: Demonetisation of the high-denomination notes was announced on 8 November 2016, with the stated aims of curbing black money, counterfeiting and corruption.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in August 2014, is primarily a programme aimed at:

options.text: financial inclusion through universal access to banking
direct income support to small and marginal farmers
affordable housing for the urban poor

explanation: PMJDY is a financial-inclusion mission providing every household access to a basic bank account, along with RuPay debit cards, overdraft facilities and insurance cover, and it underpins Direct Benefit Transfer.
subject: Economy
theme: Indian Economy after 2014 (Vivek Singh Ch 7 / NCERT)

question: The Simon Commission (1927) was widely boycotted by Indians primarily because:

options.text: it recommended the partition of India
it was an all-white commission with no Indian member
it proposed the abolition of separate electorates
it sought to dissolve the Indian National Congress

explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission, headed by Sir John Simon, contained no Indian member, which was seen as an insult to Indian self-respect and provoked nationwide protests under the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: The Nehru Report of 1928, drafted as an Indian response to the challenge to frame a constitution, was prepared by a committee chaired by:
explanation: The committee was chaired by Motilal Nehru (with Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary) and produced the Nehru Report, the first major attempt by Indians to draft a constitutional framework.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: Consider the following statements about the Nehru Report (1928): 1. It favoured dominion status as the basis of the constitution. 2. It recommended separate electorates for religious minorities. 3. It included a declaration of fundamental rights. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The Nehru Report favoured dominion status and, crucially, rejected separate electorates in favour of joint electorates (with reservation of seats in some cases), while incorporating a set of fundamental rights. Statement 2 is therefore wrong.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the:
explanation: The Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Salt March (Dandi March) starting 12 March 1930, when Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram to break the salt law.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)
micro_topic: Launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement

question: The Dandi March, undertaken to break the salt law, began at Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 and culminated in Gandhi making salt at Dandi on:
explanation: After a march of about 240 miles over roughly 24 days, Gandhi reached Dandi and violated the salt law by making salt on 6 April 1930, formally inaugurating the Civil Disobedience Movement.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: Consider the following statements about the three Round Table Conferences: 1. The Indian National Congress was absent from the First Round Table Conference. 2. Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Congress. 3. The Congress was absent from the Third Round Table Conference. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The Congress boycotted the First Conference (its leaders were in jail during Civil Disobedience); Gandhi attended the Second Conference as the sole Congress representative following the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; and the Congress again stayed away from the Third Conference. All three statements are correct.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 was concluded chiefly in order to:

options.text: secure Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference and suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement
implement the Communal Award of Ramsay MacDonald

explanation: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact the Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and to participate in the Second Round Table Conference, in return for the release of political prisoners and certain concessions.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)

question: The Poona Pact of 1932, concluded between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar, resulted in:

options.text: the grant of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes
reserved seats for the Depressed Classes within joint (general) electorates
the complete abolition of communal representation
the grant of dominion status to India

explanation: The Communal Award had provided separate electorates for the Depressed Classes; Gandhi's fast-unto-death led to the Poona Pact, which replaced separate electorates with a larger number of reserved seats for the Depressed Classes within joint (general) electorates.
subject: History
theme: Simon Commission to Round Table Conferences (Spectrum Ch 18-20)
micro_topic: Poona Pact and the Communal Award

question: The National Air Quality Index (AQI) tracks a set of pollutants for real-time air-quality reporting. Which of the following is NOT among the pollutants covered by the AQI?
explanation: The AQI covers eight pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, ozone, ammonia and lead. Carbon dioxide, though a greenhouse gas, is not one of the criteria pollutants in the AQI.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: 'Blue baby syndrome' (methaemoglobinaemia) in infants is associated with a high concentration of which contaminant in drinking water?
explanation: Excess nitrate in drinking water is converted to nitrite in the infant gut, impairing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and causing methaemoglobinaemia, commonly called blue baby syndrome.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: With reference to particulate matter, consider the following statements: 1. PM2.5 refers to particles with an aerodynamic diameter of less than 2.5 micrometres. 2. Finer particulate matter penetrates deeper into the respiratory tract than coarser particles. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: PM2.5 denotes particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres; being finer, they bypass the upper airways and reach the alveoli, making them more hazardous to health than coarser PM10. Both statements are correct.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: Eutrophication of a water body is primarily caused by its enrichment with:

options.text: heavy metals such as mercury and cadmium
nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus

explanation: Eutrophication results from nutrient over-enrichment (chiefly nitrogen and phosphorus from fertiliser run-off and sewage), which triggers algal blooms, oxygen depletion and death of aquatic life.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: Consider the following pollutants and their principal effects on human health or the environment: 1. Sulphur dioxide - acid rain. 2. Carbon monoxide - reduction of the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood. 3. Lead - damage to the nervous system. Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides form acids that cause acid rain; carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin more readily than oxygen, reducing oxygen transport; and lead is a neurotoxin affecting the nervous system. All three pairs are correctly matched.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: Biomagnification refers to:

options.text: the accumulation of a pollutant within a single organism over its lifetime
the increasing concentration of a persistent substance at successive trophic levels of a food chain
the rapid growth of algae in nutrient-rich waters
the dilution of pollutants in large water bodies

explanation: Biomagnification is the progressive increase in the concentration of a persistent, non-degradable substance (such as DDT or mercury) as it passes up the food chain from lower to higher trophic levels.
subject: Environment
theme: Environmental Pollution (Shankar IAS)

question: In India, the natural vegetation that develops in regions receiving annual rainfall of more than 200 cm is:
explanation: Tropical evergreen or rain forests occur in the heavy-rainfall belts (over 200 cm) such as the Western Ghats, north-eastern hills and the Andamans; they are dense, multi-layered and remain green throughout the year.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: Tropical deciduous forests, the most widespread forests of India, are also popularly known as:
explanation: Tropical deciduous forests are called monsoon forests; the trees shed their leaves for six to eight weeks in the dry season. They are the most widespread forest type in India.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: Mangrove (tidal) forests in India are most extensively developed in which of the following?
explanation: The Sundarbans, in the delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra, hosts the most extensive mangrove forests in India, dominated by the sundari tree from which the region takes its name.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: The soil formed from the weathering of basaltic lava and best suited for cotton cultivation in the Deccan is:
explanation: Black soil, or regur, formed from the weathering of Deccan basalt, is fine-textured, moisture-retentive and rich in lime, iron and magnesia, making it ideal for cotton - hence 'black cotton soil'.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: With reference to laterite soils in India, consider the following statements: 1. They develop in areas of high temperature and heavy rainfall. 2. They are generally rich in humus content. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Laterite soils form under high temperature and heavy rainfall with alternate wet and dry spells, where intense leaching removes silica and leaves iron and aluminium oxides. They are poor in humus, nitrogen, potash and lime, so statement 2 is wrong.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: Consider the following biosphere reserves and their locations: 1. Nanda Devi - Uttarakhand. 2. Nokrek - Meghalaya. 3. Similipal - Odisha. Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve lies in Uttarakhand, Nokrek in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, and Similipal in Odisha. All three pairs are correctly matched.
subject: Geography
theme: India: Natural Vegetation, Soils & Physical Environment (NCERT-11)

question: India's three-stage nuclear power programme was conceived by:
explanation: The three-stage nuclear programme was formulated by Homi J. Bhabha, aiming to use India's limited uranium and vast thorium reserves through a closed fuel cycle.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Nuclear Technology (Science & Technology)

question: The second stage of India's three-stage nuclear programme is based on which type of reactor?
explanation: Stage 1 uses Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors fuelled by natural uranium; Stage 2 uses Fast Breeder Reactors that use plutonium (from Stage 1) and breed more fissile material; Stage 3 aims at thorium-U-233 based reactors.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Nuclear Technology (Science & Technology)

question: The third stage of India's nuclear programme is designed to exploit the country's abundant reserves of:
explanation: India holds one of the world's largest thorium reserves (in monazite sands). The third stage aims to breed fissile uranium-233 from thorium, making thorium the long-term backbone of India's nuclear energy.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Nuclear Technology (Science & Technology)

question: In a nuclear fission reactor, the primary function of a moderator such as heavy water or graphite is to:

options.text: slow down fast neutrons to sustain the chain reaction

explanation: A moderator slows down fast neutrons to thermal energies at which they are more likely to cause further fission, thereby sustaining a controlled chain reaction. Control rods, by contrast, absorb neutrons to regulate the reaction.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Nuclear Technology (Science & Technology)

question: Consider the following statements: 1. Nuclear fission releases energy by splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei. 2. Nuclear fusion, which powers the Sun, releases energy by combining light nuclei. 3. Enriched uranium contains a higher proportion of the isotope uranium-235 than natural uranium. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Fission splits heavy nuclei (e.g., U-235) releasing energy; fusion combines light nuclei (e.g., hydrogen isotopes) as in the Sun; and enrichment raises the U-235 content above the roughly 0.7 per cent found in natural uranium. All three statements are correct.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Nuclear Technology (Science & Technology)

question: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in:
explanation: SAARC was established in 1985 at its first summit in Dhaka, with seven founding members (Afghanistan joined later in 2007).
subject: International Relations
theme: Contemporary South Asia & International Organisations (NCERT-12 CWP Ch 5-6)

question: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement, signed by SAARC members, came into force in:
explanation: SAFTA was signed in 2004 at the Islamabad Summit and entered into force on 1 January 2006, aiming to reduce tariffs among SAARC members.
subject: International Relations
theme: Contemporary South Asia & International Organisations (NCERT-12 CWP Ch 5-6)

question: Which of the following is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council with veto power?
explanation: The five permanent members (P-5) of the UN Security Council with veto power are the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia and China. India, Germany and Japan are aspirants, not permanent members.
subject: International Relations
theme: Contemporary South Asia & International Organisations (NCERT-12 CWP Ch 5-6)

question: Consider the following statements about the United Nations: 1. The United Nations was established in 1945. 2. Ten non-permanent members, elected for two-year terms, belong to the UN General Assembly. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The UN was founded in 1945. The ten non-permanent members elected for two-year terms belong to the Security Council, not the General Assembly (in which all member states sit). Statement 2 is therefore wrong.
subject: International Relations
theme: Contemporary South Asia & International Organisations (NCERT-12 CWP Ch 5-6)

question: Consider the following statements about UN Security Council reform: 1. India is one of the G-4 nations that jointly support each other's bids for permanent membership of the Security Council. 2. The G-4 comprises India, Brazil, Germany and Japan. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The G-4 - India, Brazil, Germany and Japan - back each other's candidature for permanent seats on an expanded Security Council. Both statements are correct.
subject: International Relations
theme: Contemporary South Asia & International Organisations (NCERT-12 CWP Ch 5-6)
